source_location: Table S11 (mmc12.xlsx), row 2:11588931:11592776:clu_53175_NA; Results 'Endometriosis risk genes with genetically driven effects on splicing in endometrium' text; Figure 6A
notes: Splicing QTL claim: exposure = excision ratio of LeafCutter intron 2:11588931:11592776:clu_53175_NA in GREB1. Representative event = lowest p_SMR among this gene's FDR<0.05 events. b_SMR 0.131722, se_SMR 0.0229739; p_SMR_multi 9.83394e-09; p_HEIDI 0.589758 (pass; nsnp_HEIDI 20); FDR 2.856e-05; Bonferroni column 5.712e-05. Top SNP rs12470971 (A1 A, A2 G, freq 0.3382): b_GWAS -0.0987, b_sQTL -0.7493. Other events at FDR<0.05: 2:11588931:11591396:clu_53175_NA (top SNP rs72772088) b_SMR -0.124353, se 0.023334, p_SMR 9.86085e-08, p_SMR_multi 9.86085e-08, p_HEIDI 0.255887 (pass), FDR 0.0001909. SMR of endometrial cis-sQTLs (206 samples; LeafCutter intron excision ratios mapped with QTLtools) on endometriosis. Results text: six splicing events in four genes significant at FDR<0.05, of which only GREB1 and WASHC3 pass HEIDI (P_HEIDI>=0.05). Methods define significance as Bonferroni P_SMR plus P_HEIDI>=0.05; Table S11 lists 39 events in 25 genes at FDR<0.2, and its fdr/bf columns track p_SMR_multi (bf/p ratio about 5,808 tests; number tested not stated in text). THISTLE-based sQTLs gave no FDR-significant SMR signal. Estimate: OR = exp(b_SMR), CI = exp(b_SMR +/- 1.96*se_SMR), converted here from Table S11 (log-odds per unit of the normalised splicing phenotype). Direction is per higher excision ratio of the named LeafCutter intron, not per higher gene expression. Outcome: Methods and Results cite the 2023 European GWAS meta-analysis (Rahmioglu, ref 17; Key resources GCST90205183, the public file without 23andMe); the Discussion cites Sapkota 2017 (ref 41) for this integration, and the paper used 23andMe data under a data-use agreement (listed for Sapkota 2017), so inclusion of 23andMe in the SMR outcome is not certain. Case/control counts not stated. Coloc not run. The paper describes the two GREB1 events as exon 15 skipping and intron excision (Fig. 6C) without saying which LeafCutter intron is which; the two introns share cluster clu_53175 and have opposite b_SMR signs. Headline: abstract names GREB1 and WASHC3 as associated with endometriosis risk through genetically regulated splicing.

exposure_source: deCODE (Ferkingstad 2021); described as pQTL study of 35,559 Icelanders, 4,907 proteins
outcome_source: Endometriosis GWAS (source not stated; SI Text S5 names sources only for the other ovary-related outcomes)
instruments_location: Not reported; SI Text S5 (eh5c00576_si_001.pdf p.3) gives selection rules only
notes: Instrument type checked at full text: two-sample cis-pQTL MR. SI Text S5: index cis-SNPs associated with ANGPTL4 at genome-wide significance (exponent not legible in the extracted SI text), within 1 Mb of ANGPTL4, LD-pruned with 1000 Genomes EUR; ORs by Wald ratio with delta-method SE, implying one SNP, but the number of SNPs is not stated. CI not printed (forest plot only). Seven ovary-related outcomes tested (ovarian cyst and PCOS from FinnGen r10, ovarian ageing from ReproGen, three ovarian cancer subtypes from GWAS Catalog, and endometriosis); no multiple-testing correction stated; P<=0.05 used. Endometriosis outcome source and size not stated, so cohorts unknown. Authors state exposure and outcome cohorts do not overlap. Other outcomes (Fig. 6F): ovarian cyst OR 1.204 P 0.066; ovarian aging 1.306 P 0.061; PCOS 1.067 P 0.423. No endometriosis-specific experiments; wet-lab work (ANGPTL4 knockdown in PFOA-treated KGN granulosa cells, mouse ovaries) concerns PFOA ovarian toxicity. Not headline: abstract and conclusion do not mention MR or endometriosis.

outcome_source: Pujol Gualdo 2025 EstBB + FinnGen female reproductive traits meta-analysis, endometriosis (N80)
instruments_location: Not listed per SNP; Supplementary Table 11 gives N_SNP and mean F only (instruments derivable from UKB-PPP with the stated rules)
source_location: Supplementary Table 11 (row FSHB, Endometriosis); Supplementary Table 12; Results text
notes: Beta 1.13299, SE 0.113626, P 2.0371e-23, FDR 9.439e-22; N_SNP 8, mean F 92.616. Weighted median beta 1.1738 (SE 0.1173, P 1.372e-23); MR-Egger beta 1.3227 (SE 0.1936, P 0.0004831), intercept -0.01851 (P 0.278); Cochran's Q 14.063 (P 0.05007); passed all filters: yes. r2<0.01 re-clumping (Supplementary Table 12): N_SNP 3, beta 1.1857, SE 0.1771, P 2.178e-11. Coloc PP4 0.993 (Supplementary Table 12). Reverse MR endometriosis -> FSHB: beta -0.05205, P 0.07584 (Supplementary Table 13). Primary MR (Supplementary Table 11): random-effects IVW, UKB-PPP cis-pQTLs (within 1 Mb of TSS, P<5e-8, clumped r2<0.1, F>10); significance FDR<0.05. MR was run on 139 protein-outcome pairs (78 proteins) carried forward from UK Biobank observational analyses; 13 pairs had endometriosis as outcome, of which FSHB and SEZ6L2 were significant. OR = exp(Beta), CI = exp(Beta +/- 1.96*SE), converted here from Supplementary Table 11 (log-odds per SD protein). Outcome: Pujol Gualdo et al. 2025 Estonian Biobank + FinnGen meta-analysis of female reproductive traits, endometriosis (N80), 19,588 cases / 213,669 controls, GCST90454213 (Supplementary Table 8); FinnGen release not stated. No independent replication (paper says so). Main text gives PP4 0.999 for FSHB-endometriosis and 0.993 for excessive menstrual bleeding; Supplementary Table 12 has the reverse (endometriosis 0.993, bleeding 0.999); table value used. Observational UKB: FSHB associated with prevalent endometriosis (beta 0.409, FDR 1.43e-3; Supplementary Table 9); incident beta -0.291, FDR 0.164 (Supplementary Table 10). FSHB also MR-linked to excessive menstruation, leiomyoma and genital polyps. Not headline: abstract names no protein, and the closing paragraph names none; FSHB-endometriosis causality is stated in the Discussion only.
